One particularly egregious factual point involved a 2021 case where Hill accepted over $14,000 from a vulnerable elderly homeowner for a roof replacement that was never even started, leaving the resident with a leaky roof and a significant financial loss. Furthermore, the Attorney General’s investigation revealed that Hill often operated without the proper liability insurance required by state law, exposing customers to immense risk should any accidents or damages have occurred on their property. This ban is part of a broader crackdown on contractor fraud in the region, especially following severe weather events when homeowners are most susceptible to making rushed decisions. The permanent injunction not only prohibits Hill from offering or performing roofing services but also mandates the payment of restitution to the identified victims, although the full recovery of lost funds is often challenging in such cases. Officials are urging consumers to always verify a contractor’s license and insurance, seek multiple bids, and be wary of those who demand large upfront payments before any materials are delivered. This case serves as a stark reminder of the importance of due diligence and the ongoing efforts by state authorities to hold dishonest businesses accountable for exploiting Kansas residents.

text: Nestled on a quiet street in the historic market town of Higham Ferrers, Northamptonshire, a modest shopfront with peeling paint and a weathered sign holds a significant, if often overlooked, place in British retail history. This unassuming building was the site of the very first British branch of what would become a global retail phenomenon: the Great Universal Stores (G.U.S.) catalogue showroom. Opened in the early 1930s, this pioneering outlet revolutionized shopping for residents in this corner of the East Midlands and laid the groundwork for a new era of consumer access. At a time when many households, particularly in rural areas, had limited access to the variety of goods available in major city department stores, the G.U.S. catalogue bridged a crucial gap. Customers could browse through extensive catalogues filled with everything from clothing and fabrics to household appliances and furniture, then place their orders directly at the Higham Ferrers shop, which served as a vital ordering and collection point. This model democratized consumption, offering choice and convenience long before the rise of modern e-commerce. The success of this initial venture was no accident; Higham Ferrers was strategically chosen due to its connection to the G.U.S. founder, Sir Isaac Wolfson, who had familial ties to the area. Furthermore, the G.U.S. operation was instrumental during the austerity of the post-World War II period, providing essential goods through its mail-order system when high-street shelves were often bare. From this single Northamptonshire shop, the G.U.S. empire expanded rapidly, eventually growing into one of the largest mail-order and retail businesses in the United Kingdom, employing tens of thousands and becoming a household name for decades. While the original shop may no longer operate and the G.U.S. name has since faded from the high street after a series of corporate demergers, its legacy is profound. It stands as a physical testament to a transformative shift in British shopping habits, a precursor to the catalogue giants like Littlewoods that followed, and a fascinating prototype for the click-and-collect retail world we know today. The OAG's statement clarified that the confiscation order was issued by the Federal Criminal Court in Bellinzona, providing a crucial judicial endorsement for the permanent removal of these assets from the control of the implicated parties. Furthermore, the office indicated that the confiscated billion dollars is intended for restitution to Venezuela, pending a formal request for international legal assistance and the establishment of a mechanism to ensure the funds benefit the Venezuelan people. This case is part of a broader global crackdown on corruption emanating from Venezuela, with authorities in the United States and other European nations having seized billions in related assets. The scale of the seizure from a single jurisdiction underscores the immense capital flight alleged to have occurred during a period of profound economic and social crisis in Venezuela. The Swiss authorities have not disclosed the identities of the individuals or entities from whom the assets were taken, citing ongoing proceedings, but the move signals a decisive step toward accountability and asset recovery in one of the world's most high-profile kleptocracy cases.

text: In a recent interview that has sparked considerable debate across the basketball world, former NBA All-Star and current Memphis Tigers head coach Penny Hardaway expressed a controversial view on Los Angeles Clippers forward Kawhi Leonard. Hardaway stated plainly that he does not consider Leonard to be a "superstar," a designation reserved in his mind for players who consistently dominate the game on a nightly basis with flash and undeniable statistical impact. He pointed to Leonard's managed load and occasional absences, suggesting that true superstars are defined by their relentless availability and leadership in carrying a team through an entire grueling season. This assessment comes despite Leonard's impeccable resume, which includes two NBA championships with two different franchises and two Finals MVP awards, accomplishments that most analysts place in the rarefied air of superstar achievement. Furthermore, Leonard is a six-time All-Star and five-time All-Defensive Team selection, credentials that underscore his two-way dominance when on the court. Hardaway's comments, while reflective of an older school mentality that prioritizes durability and nightly spectacle, inevitably clash with the modern understanding of Leonard's transformative impact, where his playoff performances and elite efficiency often overshadow regular-season pacing. title: Penny Hardaway does not think Kawhi Leonard is a superstar

text: A recent review of safety protocols has revealed that more than one in ten New Jersey Transit train engineers screened for sleep apnea tested positive for the disorder, raising significant concerns about fatigue management within the state's vital rail system. The Federal Railroad Administration has long identified sleep apnea, which causes breathing interruptions during sleep leading to daytime drowsiness, as a major safety risk for transportation workers. In response to these findings, NJ Transit has mandated that all engineers who test positive must undergo treatment, which typically involves using a CPAP machine at night to ensure restful sleep, before they can return to operating trains. The agency asserts that these engineers are not permitted to work until their treatment is successfully established and monitored. This proactive stance is part of broader efforts to enhance commuter safety, following a 2016 New Jersey Transit train crash at Hoboken Terminal that was linked to an engineer with undiagnosed severe sleep apnea. While the screening program aims to mitigate risks, it underscores the ongoing challenge of ensuring that those at the controls of massive passenger trains are fully alert and fit for duty every time they depart the station.

text: In a tense prelude to their highly anticipated Champions League semifinal second leg, Bayern Munich’s veteran manager Jupp Heynckes deftly returned the psychological pressure to Real Madrid by warning that the Spanish giants are not immune to faltering under the immense weight of expectation. Speaking at the Allianz Arena ahead of the crucial match, Heynckes, who famously led Real Madrid to their long-awaited seventh European Cup in 1998, acknowledged the quality of the reigning champions but pointedly highlighted the precarious nature of their one-goal aggregate lead. He suggested that Madrid, despite their formidable reputation and the presence of stars like Cristiano Ronaldo, would feel the strain of protecting a narrow 2-1 advantage in a stadium known for its intimidating atmosphere. This strategic comment shifts the narrative from Bayern’s must-win desperation to a scenario where Madrid, perhaps subconsciously, could adopt a cautious approach, thereby playing into the hands of a Bayern side that must attack. Heynckes bolstered his point by referencing the historical context of the competition, noting that comebacks are a staple of its lore and that no lead is ever truly safe, especially against a team of Bayern’s caliber. Factually, the tie remains finely balanced, with Bayern needing to win by at least a one-goal margin to force extra time, provided they outscore Madrid by two clear goals to advance directly. By calmly issuing this warning, the 73-year-old tactician has masterfully reframed the contest, reminding everyone that the eleven-time European champions, for all their pedigree, now face a monumental test of nerve in Munich, where a single Bayern goal could radically alter the complexion of the entire tie and expose any latent vulnerability in Zinedine Zidane’s squad.

text: OTTAWA – Foreign Affairs Minister Chrystia Freeland is laying out Canada’s core foreign policy principles in a defining speech that frames a world increasingly divided between democracies and authoritarian states. Furthermore, Freeland underscored the critical importance of international alliances, explicitly highlighting Canada’s deep integration within the NATO framework and its active role in the Indo-Pacific, where the government has committed $2.3 billion to enhance regional security and foster deeper trade ties. Her vision connects global engagement directly to domestic prosperity, asserting that protecting the international rules that allow for free and fair trade is essential for the economic well-being of Canadian workers and businesses. This approach, she contended, requires robust investments in national defense and cybersecurity while simultaneously building resilient supply chains with trusted democratic partners. Freeland’s articulation of Canada’s core interests presents a foreign policy that is neither isolationist nor merely reactive, but proactively engaged in shaping a coalition of nations committed to collective security, human rights, and shared economic resilience in an uncertain geopolitical landscape.
title: OTTAWA – Foreign Affairs Minister Chrystia Freeland is laying out Canada’s core

text: WASHINGTON (AP) — Supreme Court Justice Neil Gorsuch wasn’t shy Monday about making his skepticism known regarding the legal doctrine of "Chevron deference," a foundational administrative law principle that directs courts to defer to federal agencies' reasonable interpretations of ambiguous statutes. During oral arguments in a pair of cases challenging a National Marine Fisheries Service rule, Gorsuch, joined by several colleagues, voiced deep concerns that the four-decade-old precedent concentrates too much power in the executive branch and undermines the judiciary's duty to say what the law is. The cases, *Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo* and *Relentless, Inc. v. Department of Commerce*, specifically question whether fishermen can be required to pay for onboard monitors, but the court's conservative majority appeared broadly focused on the opportunity to overturn or significantly curtail the Chevron framework. Gorsuch, whose mother, Anne Gorsuch Burford, led the Environmental Protection Agency under President Ronald Reagan, has long been a vocal critic of the doctrine, arguing it allows agencies to flip-flop on regulations with changing presidential administrations and leaves individuals and businesses subject to unpredictable rules. A decision to overturn Chevron would represent a monumental shift in the balance of power among the branches of government, potentially leading to a surge of litigation as courts reexamine a wide array of existing regulations on everything from environmental protection to consumer safety and telecommunications. The justices are expected to issue their ruling in these closely watched cases by the end of the court's term in late June or early July.

text: Yellowstone National Park, established in 1872 as the world’s first national park, is one of the most remarkable places on the planet. This sprawling wilderness, spanning parts of Wyoming, Montana, and Idaho, is a living testament to the raw power and beauty of the natural world. Its landscape is dominated by the Yellowstone Caldera, one of the largest active supervolcanoes on Earth, which fuels over ten thousand hydrothermal features. Among these are the iconic Old Faithful geyser, which erupts with impressive regularity, and the Grand Prismatic Spring, a breathtaking hot spring renowned for its vibrant, rainbow-like colors. Beyond its geothermal wonders, the park serves as a crucial sanctuary for wildlife, including the largest concentration of mammals in the lower 48 states, such as grizzly bears, wolves, and free-roaming bison herds. This unique combination of volatile geology, pristine ecosystems, and awe-inspiring vistas solidifies Yellowstone’s status as a global treasure and a profound reminder of our planet’s dynamic history.
title: Yellowstone is one of the most remarkable places on the planet.

title: Hamilton Mountain Coun. Terry Whitehead is once again considering a run for mayo

text:
Bangkok Bank, Thailand's largest lender by assets, reported a marginal year-on-year decline in its first-quarter net profit, a result that underscores the persistent challenges within the domestic economy despite a gradual rise in interest rates. The bank announced a net profit of 10.3 billion baht (approximately $280 million) for the January-March period, a slight decrease of 0.15 percent from the 10.32 billion baht recorded in the same quarter last year. This near-stagnant performance, coming amid a cycle of monetary policy tightening by the Bank of Thailand, reflects a complex operating environment where higher lending rates have not fully translated into significantly improved net interest margins. Analysts point to intense competition in the loan market and cautious borrowing by businesses as key factors tempering growth. A notable bright spot, however, was a significant reduction in provisions for expected credit losses, which fell by 36.5 percent from the previous quarter, suggesting a more optimistic outlook on asset quality and potential credit risks. This prudent management of reserves provided a crucial buffer against other pressures on profitability.

The bank's core lending business showed measured expansion, with total loans increasing by 1.3 percent from the end of 2023, primarily driven by growth in corporate and commercial lending. However, this was partially offset by a contraction in retail loans, indicating continued consumer prudence. On the deposit side, the bank saw a 2.1 percent increase, reflecting its strong retail base. The net interest margin (NIM), a critical gauge of lending profitability, stood at 2.31 percent, showing resilience but also highlighting the competitive and cost-sensitive landscape where funding expenses remain elevated. Looking ahead, Bangkok Bank's management has maintained a cautiously optimistic stance for the remainder of the fiscal year, acknowledging external uncertainties while emphasizing a strategic focus on supporting corporate clients, particularly those involved in regional trade and supply chain diversification. The bank's performance is often viewed as a bellwether for the Thai economy, and this latest quarterly result paints a picture of an institution navigating a path of stable, yet subdued, growth as it balances the opportunities of economic recovery with the realities of a still-fragile domestic demand and global economic volatility.
title: * Top lender Bangkok Bank Q1 profit down 0.15 pct yr/yr

text: In a welcome sign of resilience for the global economy, China's factory activity expanded at its most robust pace in eight months during February, driven by stronger domestic and external demand as production and new orders surged. The official manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI), a key gauge of factory activity, rose to 50.9 from 50.4 in January, firmly above the 50-point mark that separates expansion from contraction. This marks the second consecutive month of improving conditions and the highest reading since June of the previous year, suggesting that the world's second-largest economy is gaining momentum following the post-pandemic recovery period. The data, released by the National Bureau of Statistics, highlights a broad-based improvement with the sub-index for production jumping to 52.5 and the new orders index climbing to 51.4. Notably, the new export orders sub-index also moved into expansionary territory for the first time in over a year, indicating a tentative recovery in global trade appetite which bodes well for international supply chains. This acceleration is partly attributed to proactive government stimulus measures and a modest uptick in consumer confidence ahead of the Lunar New Year holiday, which typically sees a pre-festival procurement rush. However, analysts caution that the sustainability of this growth remains under scrutiny, as the property sector continues to be a significant drag and broader deflationary pressures persist. The positive figures provide policymakers with some breathing room as they navigate structural economic challenges and aim to hit an ambitious growth target of around 5% for 2024. This manufacturing rebound, if sustained, could have positive ripple effects across Asian economies and commodity markets reliant on Chinese industrial demand, offering a counterweight to lingering concerns over weak domestic consumption and local government debt. The coming months will be critical in determining whether this represents a genuine turning point or a temporary holiday-induced boost, but for now, the faster expansion offers a glimmer of optimism for both Chinese and global economic prospects.

text: KEARNS, Utah — Canada’s Ted-Jan Bloemen set a world record Sunday on the final day of the World Cup speed skating event at the Utah Olympic Oval, etching his name once more into the sport's history books. The 37-year-old long-distance specialist, a two-time Olympic medalist, shattered the previous mark in the men's 10,000 meters with a stunning time of 12 minutes, 33.86 seconds. This performance clipped a substantial 2.89 seconds off the former record of 12:36.72, which had been set by Dutch legend Nils van der Poel at the same high-altitude venue in 2021. Bloemen’s achievement was a masterclass in pacing and endurance, as he navigated the grueling 25-lap race with consistent splits, ultimately crossing the line to a roaring ovation from the crowd. The record caps a remarkable comeback narrative for the Dutch-born skater, who switched allegiance to Canada in 2014 and overcame significant health challenges, including a battle with Lyme disease that hampered his training in recent seasons. His victory also underscored the Utah Oval's reputation as the world's fastest ice, a track known for its thin air and optimal conditions that have facilitated numerous world records since the 2002 Olympics. Bloemen’s record-breaking skate provided a dramatic conclusion to the World Cup weekend and sends a powerful message as he builds momentum toward the next winter games. It marks his second world record in the 10,000-meter distance, having first broken the record in 2018, and solidifies his status as one of the greatest endurance skaters of his generation. The accomplishment not only adds a significant highlight to his illustrious career but also reinvigorates Canadian hopes in the long-distance events heading into future international competitions.

text: When the founders of SpaceX first declared their ambition to make humanity a multi-planetary species, a common refrain from critics within the aerospace establishment was, "They said we were crazy." The space industry had long been the domain of governments, with private companies facing astronomical costs and high-profile failures. Yet, undeterred by early setbacks, including three consecutive launch failures that nearly bankrupted the company, SpaceX achieved a pivotal milestone in 2008 with the successful orbit of its Falcon 1 rocket. This perseverance fundamentally altered the economics of spaceflight. Today, the company’s reusable Falcon 9 rockets dominate commercial launches, and its Starship prototype represents the most powerful rocket ever built, actively being developed for future Mars missions. What once seemed like a quixotic fantasy is now driving a new era of space exploration, proving that transformative visions often begin by challenging conventional wisdom.

The team confirmed an investigation was already underway, with initial suspicions pointing toward a mechanical issue within the brake assembly itself rather than a systems telemetry failure. With the competitive field appearing closer this year, any setback in track time is costly, and Verstappen will be hoping the team can not only rebuild the car but also identify and rectify the root cause to prevent a recurrence in the high-speed, street-circuit challenge that Jeddah presents. text: In a significant advancement for electrical infrastructure safety, PSM has introduced its innovative Latching Water Level Indicator, a device designed to provide early and reliable warnings of flooding in critical sub-station environments. This robust system addresses a persistent vulnerability in power distribution networks, where unchecked water ingress can lead to catastrophic equipment failure, prolonged outages, and severe safety hazards for personnel. The indicator’s core mechanism utilizes a magnetic float switch that, once triggered by rising water, latches into an alarm state. This latching feature is crucial, as it ensures the alert remains active even if water levels temporarily recede, preventing missed warnings and guaranteeing that maintenance teams are notified of a breach. Field data from pilot installations has demonstrated the system’s effectiveness in harsh conditions, with units reliably operating in turbid water and remaining functional after extended periods of dormancy. By integrating with existing supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems, the indicator provides remote, real-time status updates, allowing for swift intervention before damage escalates. The implementation of such technology is becoming increasingly vital as climate change contributes to more frequent and severe weather events, placing greater stress on underground and ground-level electrical facilities. PSM’s solution not only protects multi-million-dollar assets from corrosive water damage but, more importantly, enhances grid resilience and public safety by preventing the kind of substation failures that can plunge entire communities into darkness. This proactive approach to infrastructure monitoring represents a smart investment in reliability, potentially saving utility companies substantial costs in emergency repairs and lost revenue while safeguarding the continuity of essential power services.
title: PSM’s Latching Water Level Indicator: Alerting Operators to Sub-Station Flooding

text: In a revelation that confirms what many schoolchildren have long suspected, scientists have announced that the planet Uranus indeed stinks. Recent spectroscopic analysis of the cloud tops, conducted using data from the Gemini North telescope in Hawaii, has detected the chemical signature of hydrogen sulfide, the gas responsible for the foul odor of rotten eggs. This discovery settles a longstanding debate about the composition of Uranus’s upper atmosphere and provides crucial clues about the formation of the solar system. The presence of hydrogen sulfide, as opposed to the ammonia more common on Jupiter and Saturn, suggests the ice giant formed much farther from the Sun in the early solar system, where conditions were colder and preserved different chemical compounds. Anyone unfortunate enough to travel through the frigid, windy clouds of Uranus would encounter not only temperatures plummeting to minus 200 degrees Celsius but also this intensely pungent and suffocating atmosphere. While the finding adds a distinctly malodorous detail to our planetary knowledge, it primarily serves as a significant piece of the puzzle in understanding the chemical gradients that existed when the planets coalesced from the primordial disk billions of years ago.
title: Newsflash: Uranus stinks!

text: A familiar yet increasingly scrutinized feature of the digital landscape, the ubiquitous countdown timer prompting users that "The video will start in 8... Cancel" represents a deliberate design choice with significant implications for user experience and online engagement. This automatic playback mechanism, employed by platforms from YouTube to various news and streaming sites, is engineered to reduce bounce rates and immediately capture viewer attention, often at the expense of user autonomy. Research into online behavior suggests that these brief windows leverage a form of decision paralysis, where the path of least resistance—allowing the video to play—is frequently taken, thereby increasing overall watch time and, consequently, advertising revenue for the host platform. Factually, the standard duration of these countdowns is not arbitrary; many are set between five and eight seconds, a period strategically chosen to be long enough for a conscious user intervention but short enough to prevent most viewers from fully disengaging. Furthermore, this practice has drawn criticism from digital rights advocates and has even prompted regulatory scrutiny in some jurisdictions, where it is viewed as potentially manipulative or a violation of user consent principles. The simple "Cancel" option, while providing a technical opt-out, is often presented with less visual prominence than the primary countdown, a subtle nudge that underscores the tension between platform design goals and genuine user choice. As the debate over ethical design intensifies, this small timer serves as a microcosm of larger conversations about attention economics and the power dynamics embedded in our everyday interactions with technology.

text: In an era defined by connectivity and convenience, the smartphone has firmly established itself as the Swiss Army knife of the digital age. text: A familiar yet often overlooked feature of the digital experience, the countdown prompt stating "The video will start in 8 Cancel" represents a critical intersection of user autonomy, platform design, and advertising revenue models. This brief window, typically lasting between five and eight seconds as standardized by the Interactive Advertising Bureau's digital video ad guidelines, serves a dual purpose. It provides viewers a mandatory period to view an advertisement while ostensibly offering a choice to skip, a design element rooted in behavioral psychology to enhance perceived control. Factually, these pre-roll ad countdowns are the backbone of the "skippable ad" format, which platforms like YouTube pioneered and which now generates billions in annual revenue by charging advertisers only when a user watches past the initial mandatory period. Furthermore, research into user experience suggests that even the presence of a "Cancel" or "Skip" option, regardless of whether it is immediately actionable, can significantly reduce negative sentiment toward forced advertising, improving overall engagement metrics. This simple timer, therefore, is far more than a minor delay; it is a carefully calibrated tool that balances monetization demands with user tolerance, shaping the economic viability of free streaming content across the web. Its ubiquitous presence underscores a fundamental trade-off in the modern media landscape: our attention is the currency, and these seconds are the transaction.
title: The video will start in 8 Cancel

text: A familiar yet often overlooked digital interface element—the countdown prompt—has become a focal point in discussions about user autonomy and design ethics. The simple message, "The video will start in 8 Cancel," represents a standard pre-roll advertisement sequence on countless websites and streaming platforms. Factually, these timers are a direct result of the 2018 Better Ads Standards established by the Coalition for Better Ads, which mandated that auto-playing ads with sound must provide a clear and easy dismissal mechanism. Furthermore, research from Nielsen Norman Group indicates that such interruptive formats, even with a cancel option, can negatively impact user perception of a brand and increase what is known as "banner blindness," where users instinctively ignore areas of a screen they associate with ads. The eight-second delay is a carefully calculated compromise, providing advertisers a guaranteed window of attention while offering a nominal, though often hurried, choice to the viewer. This design intentionally places the cognitive burden on the user to take action to stop an unwanted intrusion, a pattern critics argue prioritizes advertiser metrics over genuine consent. As the digital landscape grows more saturated, this tiny timer serves as a microcosm of the larger tension between seamless monetization and respectful user experience, prompting ongoing debate about where the line should be drawn between informed choice and manipulated engagement.

This arrest underscores the enduring reach of an operation that, though formally concluded in 2021, continues to yield new developments and legal proceedings. Gabrielli's tenure at Petrobras coincided with a period when vast kickback schemes were allegedly funneling billions from the company's coffers into political campaigns and private pockets, crippling the national economy. text: A familiar yet often overlooked digital interface element—the countdown prompt—has become the subject of both user experience scrutiny and a subtle cultural shorthand. The simple message, "The video will start in 8 Cancel," typically appears on platforms like YouTube before advertisements or featured content, giving viewers a brief window to opt out of the impending playback. This design serves a dual purpose: it provides a necessary compliance mechanism for certain types of auto-playing media, particularly ads, while also functioning as a psychological tool that can increase viewer retention by leveraging the default effect, where inaction leads to the desired outcome for the platform. Factually, the standard countdown length is often five seconds, as seen with YouTube's skippable video ads, but variations like eight seconds are implemented for different content types or platform-specific rules. Furthermore, the wording and timing of such prompts are carefully crafted to meet advertising industry standards and guidelines, such as those from the Interactive Advertising Bureau, which recommend clear user choice in auto-play scenarios. This micro-interaction encapsulates the constant negotiation for attention in the digital space, where a few seconds of delay represent a minor friction point balancing user autonomy against algorithmic curation and commercial interests. For many, the fleeting moment to hit "Cancel" has become a reflexive action, a small but definitive assertion of control in an otherwise automated viewing experience.

text: MILWAUKEE — Enes Kanter seems to play better with a stitched-up mouth. The veteran center, now with the Portland Trail Blazers, required six stitches after taking an elbow to the face during the first quarter of Wednesday night’s game against the Milwaukee Bucks. Rather than retreating to the locker room for the remainder of the contest, Kanter returned to the floor in the second quarter and proceeded to deliver a dominant performance, finishing with 11 points and a game-high 17 rebounds in a narrow 137-129 loss. This gritty display continues a curious trend for the 28-year-old; earlier this season, he played through a similar facial injury against the Sacramento Kings, logging a 14-point, 15-rebound double-double. Kanter’s resilience provided a crucial spark for a Blazers team missing starting center Jusuf Nurkic, as his relentless effort on the offensive glass generated numerous second-chance opportunities against the reigning champions. Teammates and coaches have long praised his toughness, a trait physically embodied by the protective mask he now occasionally wears. While the sample size is small, the statistical bump following these injuries is notable, suggesting a player who uses physical adversity as a catalyst for heightened focus and intensity. Kanter himself downplayed the phenomenon postgame, emphasizing his desire to simply help his team compete regardless of circumstance. Yet, as the Blazers navigate a tight playoff race in the Western Conference, they will undoubtedly hope their backup big man can channel that same stitched-up tenacity night in and night out, with or without the facial wounds.
title: MILWAUKEE — Enes Kanter seems to play better with a stitched-up mouth.

text: Residents across the region are bracing for a persistent pattern of oppressive heat and moisture as meteorologists forecast a stretch of weather best summarized as "hot and humid, with daily storms." The dominant high-pressure system, often called a "heat dome," is trapping warm, moist air at the surface, creating conditions ripe for daily afternoon and evening thunderstorms. This phenomenon is a classic feature of summer in many areas, where the intense daytime heating provides the instability needed for storm development. One key factual point is the significant role of atmospheric moisture, measured by dew points, which are expected to remain consistently in the sticky mid-70s. When dew points exceed 70 degrees Fahrenheit, the air feels tropical and oppressive, making it difficult for the human body to cool itself efficiently through perspiration. This elevates the risk for heat-related illnesses, prompting health officials to advise limiting strenuous outdoor activity during peak afternoon hours and ensuring adequate hydration. Furthermore, while the storms will provide temporary relief from the heat, they carry their own hazards. These pop-up storms are often capable of producing frequent lightning, gusty winds, and torrential downpours that can quickly lead to localized flash flooding, especially in urban areas with poor drainage. Another important consideration is the cumulative effect of these daily downpours. Over-saturated soils from repeated storms increase the risk of trees becoming uprooted in strong winds and can exacerbate flooding concerns as the week progresses. The pattern shows little sign of breaking in the immediate future, with forecast models indicating the hot, unstable air mass will remain entrenched for at least the next five to seven days. Commuters are advised to stay weather-aware for rapidly changing conditions during the evening rush hour, and gardeners might find their schedules dictated by the predictable, yet unpredictable, nature of these daily convective events. Ultimately, this week’s weather serves as a potent reminder of summer’s dual capacity for simmering stillness and sudden, violent release.
title: Hot and Humid, with Daily Storms

text: The unpredictable and often unwelcome presence of hecklers is a time-honored, if universally dreaded, aspect of the live comedy experience. For comedians, navigating these disruptive audience members is less an occasional hazard and more a fundamental part of the job description, a skill as crucial as timing or writing a punchline. This adversarial dynamic is woven into the very fabric of stand-up history, with legends like Don Rickles building a career on aggressive crowd work that often preempted hecklers, while others, like the late great Richard Pryor, could silence a disruptive patron with a single, withering glance. Factually, the phenomenon is so prevalent that a 2012 study published in the journal "Motivation and Emotion" by psychologist Peter McGraw examined audience responses and suggested that heckling can sometimes arise from a misguided desire for social connection or a bid for status within the crowd. Furthermore, the legal landscape generally offers comedians little protection, as heckling is typically considered protected free speech, leaving the resolution of these conflicts to the performer's wit and the venue's discretion. The modern era has added new dimensions to this age-old struggle, with comedians now frequently facing the added pressure of having their every off-the-cuff response recorded on smartphones and dissected online, often devoid of the heckler’s original provocation. Consequently, a comedian’s ability to deftly handle, or even creatively destroy, a heckler has become a celebrated art form in itself, with viral clips of devastating put-downs often boosting a performer’s profile. Ultimately, while audiences and artists alike may groan at the first shouted interruption, this tense interplay underscores the raw, unscripted vitality of live comedy—a high-wire act where the crowd is not always a passive observer, but sometimes an unwilling participant in the night’s unpredictable drama.
title: When it comes to comedy shows, hecklers come with the territory.

text: LOS ANGELES — In a significant move to address the city's intertwined crises of homelessness and housing affordability, Mayor Karen Bass announced a major expansion of her signature "Inside Safe" initiative on Tuesday, aiming to clear several long-standing encampments and place hundreds more individuals into temporary motel rooms. The program, which has housed over 2,200 people since its launch in December 2022, represents the city's most concerted effort to move people indoors voluntarily, though it has faced scrutiny over its long-term sustainability and cost. This latest phase will focus on areas around the city's sprawling freeway system, where an estimated 75,000 people experience homelessness on any given night in Los Angeles County, a number that has grown dramatically in recent years despite billions in public spending. The announcement comes as the city grapples with the economic pressures of being one of the nation's most expensive rental markets, where the median price for a one-bedroom apartment exceeds $2,400 per month, placing immense strain on low-income residents. Officials emphasized that this encampment resolution effort is coupled with intensified outreach to connect participants with permanent supportive housing and vital services, a critical component often cited by advocates as the key to lasting success. The challenge remains daunting, with the scale of need continually outpacing new housing production, but city leaders frame this targeted action as a necessary step toward reclaiming public spaces and delivering on promises of compassionate intervention. The operation will involve coordinated teams from multiple city departments and is scheduled to begin in the Echo Park and Venice areas within the coming weeks.

text: As drivers across the country prepare for holiday road trips, they are encountering a significant and unwelcome surge at the pump, with gasoline prices spiking to a four-year seasonal high. According to data from the Energy Information Administration, the national average for a gallon of regular unleaded has climbed sharply in recent weeks, now sitting well above the price points seen during the same period over the past three years. This upward trend is being driven by a confluence of factors, including rising global crude oil costs as OPEC+ nations maintain production cuts, which constrict supply on the international market. Furthermore, domestic refinery issues and the annual switch to more expensive summer-grade fuel, designed to reduce evaporation in warmer weather, have added substantial pressure on wholesale gasoline prices. Analysts note that while demand remains robust, the constrained supply chain is the primary culprit, creating a classic economic squeeze just as the busy summer driving season commences. The financial pinch is particularly acute for families budgeting for Memorial Day getaways, with some regions, especially the West Coast and parts of the Midwest, experiencing averages far exceeding the national figure. This development threatens to act as an inflationary force, potentially dampening consumer spending in other areas as more of the household budget is allocated to transportation. While some relief is possible after the holiday peak, market volatility linked to geopolitical tensions and hurricane season's potential impact on Gulf Coast refineries suggests that elevated prices may be a persistent feature of the summer landscape, casting a shadow over traditional seasonal travel.
title: Transcript for Holiday gas prices spike to 4-year high

text: A New York City resident has died after contracting meningococcal disease, a serious bacterial illness commonly spread through close personal contact such as coughing, kissing, or sharing drinks. The city’s health department confirmed the fatality, noting it is part of an increase in cases observed over the past year, which officials have described as the largest local outbreak in decades. Meningococcal disease, caused by the bacterium *Neisseria meningitidis*, can lead to meningitis—a dangerous inflammation of the protective membranes covering the brain and spinal cord—as well as bloodstream infections. While the disease can be severe and progress rapidly, it is not as contagious as viruses that cause the common cold or flu; transmission requires direct exchange of respiratory or throat secretions, often through prolonged close contact. Health authorities stress that vaccination offers the best protection, with vaccines routinely recommended for adolescents and certain at-risk groups, including those with compromised immune systems or travelers to regions where the disease is more common. The recent death underscores the critical importance of recognizing early symptoms, which can initially resemble flu—such as fever, headache, and stiff neck—but may swiftly worsen to include nausea, vomiting, increased sensitivity to light, and a distinctive rash. The New York City Department of Health and Mental Hygiene has urged healthcare providers to maintain a high index of suspicion and to promptly report any suspected cases to facilitate rapid public health intervention. This incident occurs amid a broader national conversation about vaccine uptake and the resurgence of preventable diseases in various communities. While the identity of the deceased has not been released, the department continues to investigate potential contacts and is emphasizing preventative measures, particularly in congregate settings. Public health experts note that despite its rarity, meningococcal disease carries a high fatality rate, with about one in ten infected individuals dying even with antibiotic treatment, making awareness and prophylaxis essential tools in curbing its spread.

text: In a significant development for the field of archaeology, Dr. Alistair McCrackin, a renowned figure whose career has been dedicated to unraveling the mysteries of ancient Near Eastern civilizations, has been awarded the prestigious Kensington Medal for lifetime achievement. McCrackin, pictured in 2006 during the excavation of a Hittite settlement in central Turkey, is an archaeologist whose meticulous fieldwork and groundbreaking publications have fundamentally reshaped academic understanding of early Iron Age trade networks. His most cited contribution remains the 1998 monograph "Trade Routes and Tribal Alliances," which compellingly argued for a much more complex and interconnected Anatolian plateau than previously theorized, based on a decade of ceramic and cuneiform evidence he helped to unearth. Beyond his scholarly work, McCrackin has been a pivotal figure in cultural heritage preservation, frequently advising UNESCO on conservation projects and publicly advocating for the protection of sites in conflict zones, a role that has earned him international respect beyond academia. The award committee specifically highlighted his mentorship of two generations of archaeologists, many of whom now lead their own digs across the Mediterranean and the Middle East, ensuring his methodological rigor and passion for the discipline carry forward. The Kensington Medal, awarded only once every five years, recognizes not only a record of discovery but also the profound and lasting impact of an individual's work on both the academic community and the public's engagement with history. Colleagues describe McCrackin, now semi-retired but still active as a senior research fellow at the Institute for Advanced Study, as a humble yet fiercely dedicated scholar for whom every fragment of pottery tells a story of human endeavor. This honor serves as a fitting capstone to a career spent not just in the dust of excavation trenches, but in building enduring bridges between the ancient past and our modern understanding of cultural development.

text: In an era of information overload, the simple act of subscribing to a newsletter has become a cornerstone of modern media consumption, offering a curated lifeline to trusted content. The familiar call to action, "Get daily updates directly to your inbox + Subscribe Thank you for subscribing!", represents more than just a website form; it signifies a direct and permission-based channel between publishers and their audience. This model has seen substantial growth, with a 2022 study indicating that for many businesses, email newsletters drive more engagement and conversion than social media platforms, boasting an average open rate of around 21%. The direct-to-inbox delivery ensures that updates bypass the unpredictable algorithms of social feeds, giving readers consistent access to the topics they care about, from breaking news and in-depth analysis to personalized product recommendations. Furthermore, the immediate "Thank you for subscribing!" confirmation is a critical touchpoint in user experience, acknowledging the user's action and often setting expectations for the type and frequency of content they will receive. This streamlined process from sign-up to confirmation underscores a shift towards owned media, where organizations can foster a dedicated community without intermediary platforms. For the subscriber, it translates to convenience and control, consolidating essential information into a single, manageable space. As digital landscapes become increasingly fragmented, the humble email newsletter, initiated by that straightforward subscription prompt, remains a remarkably resilient and effective tool for staying informed, proving that sometimes the most traditional digital methods are the most enduring.
title: Get daily updates directly to your inbox + Subscribe Thank you for subscribing!

text: The rollout of 5G technology represents far more than a simple speed upgrade for our smartphones; it is poised to be a foundational shift that will reshape industries and redefine connectivity. This next-generation network, now being deployed globally, promises not just faster downloads but ultra-low latency and the capacity to connect a massive number of devices simultaneously. These technical leaps are what elevate 5G from an incremental improvement to a genuinely transformative force. One key factual point is its projected economic impact: a landmark study by Qualcomm forecasts that by 2035, 5G will enable up to $13.2 trillion worth of goods and services, fueling innovation across the global economy. This potential is rooted in its ability to support critical applications far beyond consumer internet access. For instance, in manufacturing, the near-instantaneous response time of 5G networks will allow for the precise, real-time control of robotics and machinery, enabling truly smart factories where production lines can be reconfigured dynamically. Furthermore, the healthcare sector stands to be revolutionized through reliable remote surgeries, where a surgeon could operate on a patient miles away using robotic tools controlled over a 5G link without perceptible delay. The infrastructure itself is also evolving, utilizing a broader spectrum of radio frequencies, including high-band millimeter waves that offer blazing speeds over short distances, which will be crucial for dense urban areas and stadiums. However, this expansion is not without challenges, including the need for a denser network of antennas and ongoing discussions about infrastructure costs and digital equity. Despite these hurdles, the direction is clear. From autonomous vehicles communicating with each other and city infrastructure to create safer roads, to the seamless integration of augmented reality in both work and leisure, 5G is the essential pipeline for the data-driven future. It is the necessary backbone for the Internet of Things to reach its full potential, connecting everything from city streetlights to agricultural sensors in a cohesive, intelligent web. While the full societal transformation will unfold over the coming decade, the groundwork being laid today confirms that 5G is not just an upgrade—it is going to be a really big deal, setting the stage for a new era of technological integration and economic opportunity.
title: 5G is going to be a really big deal.

His arrest highlights the challenging transition some athletes face after their professional sports careers conclude, a narrative far too common yet no less jarring when the details involve such a massive quantity of illegal substances. According to police reports, the traffic stop was initiated for a minor violation, but the subsequent discovery of the drugs, packaged in multiple large duffel bags, escalated the situation dramatically. The sheer volume seized—equivalent to over 71 kilograms—points not to personal use but to large-scale distribution, placing Robinson in a severe legal predicament that could result in significant prison time. His story serves as a cautionary tale, a dramatic fall from the promise of a professional athlete drafted to catch passes in MetLife Stadium to a man apprehended on a highway with a van laden with contraband. The Giants' selection of Robinson, a raw prospect from the University of Cincinnati, was always considered a project, but his inability to develop into a reliable player made his tenure a footnote of disappointment for the franchise. text: In a 2014 file photo, a U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer stands in uniform, a visual artifact from an era of evolving immigration policy. The agency, established in 2003 under the newly formed Department of Homeland Security following the 9/11 attacks, consolidated immigration enforcement and investigative functions that were previously scattered across different departments. At the time the photo was taken, ICE was operating under the directives of the Obama administration, which prioritized the removal of individuals with criminal convictions, leading to a record number of deportations that exceeded 2 million during his two terms. The image serves as a reminder of the ongoing and often contentious national debate over enforcement strategies, detention practices, and the humanitarian aspects of immigration law. ICE's mission encompasses a broad range of responsibilities, including combating human trafficking, preventing the illegal movement of goods and people across borders, and targeting transnational criminal organizations. The visual of an officer from a decade ago underscores how the agency's public profile and operational focus can shift significantly with changing presidential administrations, while its core mandate of enforcing federal laws governing border control, customs, trade, and immigration remains a constant and complex challenge.
title: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer in a file photo from 2014

text:
In a significant escalation of the probe into Russian interference in the 2016 election, the Washington Post reported that Special Counsel Robert Mueller is now investigating President Donald Trump for possible obstruction of justice. This development, confirmed by multiple officials familiar with the expanding inquiry, marks a pivotal moment as it shifts the focus directly onto the President’s own actions in the aftermath of the FBI’s investigation. The obstruction examination is said to center on a series of events following Trump’s dismissal of FBI Director James Comey in May, including the President’s alleged efforts to pressure Comey to end the investigation into former National Security Advisor Michael Flynn. Furthermore, investigators are scrutinizing Trump’s reported role in crafting a misleading initial statement about a 2016 meeting at Trump Tower between his son, campaign officials, and a Russian lawyer offering damaging information on Hillary Clinton.

The investigation into obstruction stems from a pattern of behavior that prosecutors believe may have been intended to impede the broader Russia inquiry. A key factual point underscoring the seriousness of the probe is the existence of contemporaneous memos written by the ousted Director Comey, which detailed his uncomfortable interactions with the President. In one such memo, Comey recounted that Trump told him, “I hope you can see your way clear to letting this go, to letting Flynn go,” a statement now viewed as potential evidence of an attempt to influence an ongoing investigation. This inquiry operates alongside Mueller’s core mandate to examine any links between the Trump campaign and the Russian government, a sweeping investigation that has already resulted in several indictments and guilty pleas from former campaign aides. The President has repeatedly denounced the investigation as a “witch hunt,” asserting there was “no obstruction” and maintaining there was “no collusion” with Russia. Legal experts note that while a sitting president’s immunity from indictment remains an untested constitutional question, findings of obstruction could form the basis for articles of impeachment, placing immense political pressure on Congress. As Mueller’s team continues to interview key administration officials and gather evidence, the obstruction investigation ensures that the legal and political cloud over the White House will persist, fundamentally shaping the remainder of Trump’s presidency.
title: Trump Under Investigation by Special Counsel Mueller for Obstruction of Justice

text: The entertainment landscape continues to evolve at a breakneck pace, and one of the most significant shifts has been the gradual sunset of the SHOWTIME linear cable channel as a standalone entity. In a strategic move reflecting broader industry trends, Paramount Global has been methodically integrating the storied SHOWTIME brand into its flagship streaming service, Paramount+. This integration, largely completed throughout 2023, has resulted in the rebranding of the premium streaming tier to "Paramount+ with SHOWTIME," effectively making the iconic SHOWTIME name a content pillar within a larger platform rather than a separate destination. This decision underscores the intense pressure in the streaming market to consolidate content libraries and simplify consumer choices in an era of subscription fatigue. For decades, SHOWTIME stood as a hallmark of premium cable, renowned for its bold, award-winning original programming that often pushed creative boundaries. Its legacy includes groundbreaking series such as "Homeland," which garnered critical acclaim and multiple Emmy Awards, and "Dexter," a cultural phenomenon that redefined the antihero drama. Furthermore, the network has a rich history in boxing and combat sports, having broadcast historic fights for over three decades, including the early bouts of Mike Tyson. While these classic titles and new SHOWTIME-originated series like "The Chi" and "Yellowjackets" continue to be produced and housed under the SHOWTIME banner on Paramount+, the standalone app has been phased out. This transition has not been without its challenges, involving careful migration of subscriber accounts and content libraries, and it signals a definitive end to an era where premium cable channels operated as siloed empires. The move is a clear acknowledgment that in today's crowded digital arena, scale and a unified content portfolio are paramount for survival. For viewers, it means accessing a vast combined library from a single point, but it also marks the fading of a distinct brand that once represented a specific tier of television artistry. The show, as they say, must go on, but for SHOWTIME, it now does so on a much larger and more competitive stage.
title: SHOWTIME

text: While the NFL playoffs narrow the field to a handful of teams, the world of fantasy football is far from dormant. For millions of enthusiasts, the action simply shifts to daily fantasy sports (DFS) contests, which continue to offer weekly competitions throughout the postseason. This seamless transition allows managers to build new lineups each week from the remaining playoff teams, focusing on single-game or weekend-long contests rather than season-long leagues. A key factual point is the significant economic footprint of this trend; the Fantasy Sports & Gaming Association reports that nearly 45 million people in the U.S. and Canada played fantasy sports in 2022, with a substantial portion engaged in DFS formats. Platforms like DraftKings and FanDuel see sustained traffic, as the condensed playoff schedule creates intense, high-stakes decision-making centered on star performances in win-or-go-home scenarios. Furthermore, the single-elimination nature of the playoffs introduces unique strategic layers, as managers must weigh a player’s potential for a massive game against the risk of his team suffering an early exit. This ensures the fantasy community remains deeply engaged, analyzing matchups and injury reports with the same fervor they did in September, proving that for a dedicated cohort, the fantasy football season only truly ends after the Super Bowl’s final whistle.
title: In playoffs, fantasy football keeps rolling with daily contests If there is one

text: Serena Williams, whose legendary tennis career includes 23 Grand Slam singles titles and a record-setting seven Wimbledon championships, is married to Alexis Ohanian, a prominent technology entrepreneur and venture capitalist. The couple, who first met in 2015 and married in a lavish New Orleans ceremony in 2017, represent a powerful union of sports and Silicon Valley. Ohanian is best known as the co-founder of the social news aggregation platform Reddit, a website that grew into a cornerstone of internet culture and was valued in the billions. Beyond this flagship achievement, he is also a founding partner of the venture capital firm Initialized Capital, which has invested in numerous successful tech startups. Their relationship, often shared with fans on social media, is centered on a strong partnership and mutual support, with Ohanian frequently seen cheering from the player’s box during Williams’ historic matches, including her final appearances at Wimbledon before stepping back from tennis to focus on family and business ventures. Together, they are parents to daughter Olympia, born in 2017, and Ohanian has been an outspoken advocate for women’s equality, famously pledging significant investment in female-founded companies. The marriage blends Williams’ global athletic stardom with Ohanian’s influential role in the tech industry, creating a family dynamic that is both intensely private in its core values yet publicly inspirational in its demonstration of shared ambition and parenting. Their story continues to captivate, not just as a celebrity narrative, but as a modern tale of two high-achieving individuals building a life beyond their respective courts.
title: Who is Serena Williams’ husband Alexis Ohanian? Wimbledon tennis star’s marriage

text: The enigmatic em dash—this versatile punctuation mark has quietly become a cornerstone of modern writing, offering a dynamic alternative to more formal commas, colons, and parentheses. Its primary function is to create a strong break in a sentence, often used to insert a clarifying thought, an emphatic aside, or a dramatic pause that commas alone cannot convey. Linguistically, it differs from its shorter cousins, the hyphen and the en dash; a hyphen joins compound words, an en dash indicates ranges like "pages 10–15," while the em dash—so named because it was historically the width of a capital M in printing—serves these more interruptive roles. Its adoption has surged in digital communication, particularly in blogs and online journalism, where its informal and emphatic quality helps mimic the rhythm of spoken language. However, traditional style guides like *The Chicago Manual of Style* recommend using it sparingly to maintain clarity and avoid a cluttered appearance, a cautionary note often overlooked in more casual prose. Despite its seemingly simple appearance, the em dash carries significant stylistic weight, allowing writers to inject personality, control pacing, and highlight crucial information with a single stroke. Its rise reflects a broader trend in writing towards more conversational and expressive forms, proving that even the smallest marks can powerfully shape meaning and tone on the page.

From our correspondent in Geneva, the World Health Organization has released a new report warning of a significant and accelerating threat from antimicrobial resistance. The analysis, compiling data from 127 countries, indicates that bacterial infections are becoming increasingly untreatable by common antibiotics, directly contributing to over 1.2 million deaths annually. This silent pandemic, driven by the overuse and misuse of antimicrobials in both human medicine and agriculture, is eroding a cornerstone of modern healthcare. Health officials stress that without immediate and coordinated global action, routine medical procedures like surgeries and cancer treatments could become far more dangerous due to the risk of untreatable infections. The WHO is now calling for increased investment in the development of new antibiotics and for all nations to implement stricter stewardship programs to preserve the efficacy of existing drugs. The findings underscore a critical juncture for public health systems worldwide, demanding a unified response to a crisis that transcends borders.
title: By our correspondent

text: In a move signaling ambitious intent, AC Milan have appointed Cesc Fàbregas as the new head coach of their Under-19 Primavera side, tasking the legendary former midfielder with igniting a revolution at the club's famed youth academy. The 37-year-old, who enjoyed a storied playing career with Arsenal, Barcelona, Chelsea, and Monaco, recently completed his UEFA Pro License and will now begin his first major coaching role. His appointment is seen as a strategic effort to bridge the gap between Milan's youth setup and the first team, instilling a modern, possession-based philosophy from the ground up. Fàbregas, who won the 2010 World Cup and two European Championships with Spain, brings a wealth of top-level experience and a deep understanding of the game that the Rossoneri hierarchy believes is crucial for developing the next generation of talent. This foundational shift aims to restore Milan's tradition of producing homegrown stars, creating a sustainable pipeline for future success at the San Siro.
title: Fabregas to start Milan revolution

text: The quiet residential street of 1390 Saddle Rack St. has become the unlikely epicenter of a burgeoning community debate following the city council's narrow approval of a controversial rezoning request. For decades, the property, a modest single-family home on a sprawling one-acre lot, was a fixture in the established neighborhood. However, its recent purchase by developer Crestview Holdings has set the stage for a significant transformation, with plans submitted to demolish the existing structure and construct a multi-unit condominium complex. This proposed shift from low-density to medium-density housing has sharply divided local residents, pitting concerns over preserving neighborhood character against arguments addressing the city's acute housing shortage. Proponents of the development, including Mayor Elena Ruiz, cite a recent urban housing study that identified this quadrant of the city as critically underserved for affordable entry-level homes, a gap the 12-unit "Saddle Creek Villas" project aims to partially fill. Opponents, organized under the "Preserve Saddle Rack" banner, counter that the infrastructure, particularly the narrow street itself and the already overcrowded local elementary school, cannot sustain the projected influx of dozens of new residents and vehicles. The final council vote of 4-3, held after a marathon public comment session, hinged on a concession from the developer to fund a traffic calming study and contribute to a school district impact fund. As construction permits are now being processed, the outcome at 1390 Saddle Rack St. is being watched closely as a potential precedent for similar infill developments across the city's older suburbs.
title: 1390 Saddle Rack St.

text: Google has announced the accepted student projects for this year's Google Summer of Code, continuing its two-decade-long tradition of connecting aspiring developers with open-source organizations. This flagship initiative, which began in 2005, provides students with a stipend to write code and contribute to real-world software projects under the guidance of mentors from participating foundations. The announcement marks a key milestone, revealing the thousands of students from over 100 countries who have been selected to collaborate with hundreds of diverse open-source entities over the coming months. A notable factual point is the program's significant global reach and impact; since its inception, more than 19,000 contributors from 118 countries have participated, producing over 44 million lines of code for hundreds of organizations. This year's cohort will engage with a wide array of technologies, spanning areas like artificial intelligence, cloud computing, scientific research tools, and operating systems, contributing to foundational projects such as the Linux Kernel, Apache Software Foundation, and the Python Software Foundation. Another key detail is the program's structure, which is not a conventional internship but a remote, focused coding experience where students complete a project proposal during an application process before being matched with a mentoring organization. The selected contributors will now embark on a multi-month journey, beginning with a community bonding period followed by intensive coding, with their work culminating in final evaluations in late fall. This initiative not only fuels innovation within the open-source ecosystem but also serves as a critical pipeline for developing the next generation of software engineers, many of whom secure future employment based on their demonstrated contributions. The announcement solidifies Google's ongoing commitment to fostering open-source development and providing invaluable experiential learning that bridges academic knowledge with practical, collaborative software creation on a global scale.
title: Google has announced the accepted student projects for this year's Google Summer

text: Turkey’s top judicial body, the Council of Judges and Prosecutors (HSK), has dismissed 39 more judges and prosecutors for alleged links to the Gülen movement, which the government designates as a terrorist organization. This latest purge is part of a sweeping, years-long crackdown following the failed 2016 coup attempt, which Ankara blames on followers of the US-based cleric Fethullah Gülen. The dismissals bring the total number of jurists removed from their posts since the coup to well over 4,000, fundamentally reshaping the country's judiciary. Critics, including international human rights organizations, argue the campaign has been used to suppress dissent and erode judicial independence, while the government maintains it is a necessary measure to cleanse state institutions of security threats. The move underscores the enduring impact of the post-coup state of emergency, as the Turkish authorities continue to target perceived members of the network across all public sectors.
title: Turkey’s top judicial body dismisses 39 more judges, prosecutors over Gülen link

text: The haunting black-and-white photographs of the Holocaust have long served as a stark, historical record of unparalleled atrocity. However, a recent project utilizing advanced digital colorization techniques has rendered these images in color, making them, in the words of many historians and viewers, even more chilling and harrowing. The addition of pigment transforms scenes from a distant, monochrome past into a visceral present, where the green of a patch of grass or the ruddy hue of a brick wall collapses the decades of separation. This immediacy forces a confrontation with the reality that the victims were people living in a world as visually rich as our own, not merely figures in a historical documentary. One factual point underscoring this impact is the systematic use of color film by the Nazis themselves, most infamously in the case of the Auschwitz Album, a SS-compiled photograph collection that recorded the arrival of Hungarian Jews at the death camp in 1944. Seeing those long lines of people, with the varied colors of their coats and hats, against the bleak landscape of the camp makes the bureaucratic efficiency of the genocide horrifically tangible. Furthermore, the colorization of iconic images, such as the terrified boy with raised hands during the Warsaw Ghetto Uprising, intensifies the emotional weight; the brown of his shorts and the details of his surroundings amplify his individuality and the specific moment of his terror. Scholars note that while the original photographs remain the definitive historical documents, these colorized versions serve a powerful pedagogical purpose by bridging the emotional gap for newer generations accustomed to color media. The result is a profound and unsettling reminder that the shadows of the Holocaust were cast not in a grayscale world, but in one filled with the same vivid colors we see today, making the inhumanity depicted not an abstract historical event, but a crime that happened in a reality jarringly similar to our own.
title: These images from the Holocaust are even more chilling in color These harrowing

text: SALT LAKE CITY — Sedrick Barefield led five Utah starters in double figures with a game-high 23 points, orchestrating a balanced offensive attack that overwhelmed the opposition in a decisive home victory. The Utes' cohesive performance was evident from the opening tip, as Barefield's sharp shooting from beyond the arc opened driving lanes for his teammates. text: In a move highlighting the web’s ongoing evolution, a common message encountered by users worldwide—"Please enable Javascript to watch this video"—serves as a quiet reminder of the technology’s fundamental role in modern online experiences. While disabling JavaScript can enhance privacy and security for some advanced users, it renders many core website functions inoperable. The persistent request to enable it underscores a broader shift from static web pages to dynamic, application-like experiences, where video, complex animations, and real-time updates are standard. text:
A recent investigation has revealed a significant flaw in Twitter's content moderation systems, highlighting the platform's inability to distinguish between posts written by a user before they turned 13 and those created after. This technical shortcoming poses a serious compliance issue with the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA), a U.S. federal law that prohibits the collection of personal data from children under 13 without verifiable parental consent. Because Twitter's systems cannot accurately identify and segregate content posted during a user's pre-teen years, the platform risks indefinitely retaining data that was unlawfully collected, a violation that can carry substantial fines. This failure is particularly acute given that users who joined the platform underage and are now adults have no automated way to purge their historical, non-compliant data, leaving it embedded in Twitter's archives.

The issue underscores a broader challenge in social media governance, where age verification remains a persistent and complex problem. While platforms like Twitter require users to be at least 13 to create an account, enforcement has historically relied on self-reporting, a method easily circumvented. The platform's current architecture, which treats a user's entire tweet history as a monolithic block regardless of the age at which each post was authored, demonstrates a lack of granular age-based data filtering. This is not merely a privacy concern but also a safety one, as content posted by a child could resurface years later without context, potentially exposing them to unintended risks. Experts argue that resolving this would require a fundamental re-engineering of how social media platforms timestamp and categorize user data against age milestones, a costly and technically demanding endeavor that no major platform has yet fully implemented. As regulatory scrutiny around children's online safety intensifies globally, this specific failing places Twitter in a precarious position, forced to confront the lingering digital footprints of users who should never have been on the service in the first place.

text: LONDON (CNN) — Plenty of us turn to takeout when we’re feeling too sick to cook, a common instinct that new research suggests may be counterproductive for public health. A study published in the *Journal of Nutrition Education and Behavior* examining food delivery app usage during the COVID-19 pandemic found that orders spiked not only during lockdowns but also in correlation with local rises in influenza and other illnesses. This trend raises significant concerns among health professionals, as comfort foods often sought when unwell are typically higher in salt, sugar, and saturated fats, which can impair immune function and prolong recovery. Furthermore, the act of ordering in, while convenient, increases the risk of transmitting pathogens to delivery drivers and restaurant staff, creating a wider chain of potential exposure. Nutritionists emphasize that the body’s need for nutrient-dense foods—like broths, steamed vegetables, and lean proteins—is greatest during illness, yet these are seldom the top choices on delivery platforms. The convenience economy, valued in the hundreds of billions globally, effectively capitalizes on our moments of vulnerability, making the unhealthy choice the easiest one. This creates a dual burden: individuals may delay their own healing while inadvertently contributing to community spread of contagions. Experts advise those feeling under the weather to plan ahead by keeping simple, wholesome ingredients stocked for easy meals, thereby supporting personal health and reducing unnecessary social contacts. The findings highlight a modern paradox where technology designed to solve a problem—feeding us when we are incapacitated—may inadvertently exacerbate another, reminding us that the oldest remedies often start at home, in our own kitchens.
title: LONDON (CNN) — Plenty of us turn to takeout when we’re feeling too sick to cook.

The collaboration between the charity, the school, and filmmaking experts illustrates a potent model for creating impactful public health messaging, directly informed by the insights of those it seeks to protect. As the film rolls out, it stands as a testament to the value of listening to young people on issues that directly affect their generation, providing them not just with information but with a platform to shape the conversation. This Corby school’s success demonstrates how student innovation can transcend the classroom and contribute to a national dialogue, offering a proactive tool in the effort to safeguard youth from the hidden dangers lurking in digital spaces.

text: In an era where information overload is a constant challenge, a growing number of readers are seeking curated news delivered with convenience. The familiar follow-up message, "Thank you for subscribing!," marks the beginning of a direct and personalized information stream. This model has become a cornerstone of digital media strategy, with a 2022 study indicating that newsletter subscribers are often a publication's most engaged audience, demonstrating higher click-through and retention rates than casual visitors. The shift reflects a broader move towards audience-owned channels, as social media algorithms increasingly limit the organic reach of news organizations. By opting in, users effectively build a custom newsfeed, ensuring they receive consistent updates on topics ranging from global finance to local community events without the noise of unrelated content. Furthermore, the direct line of communication fosters a sense of connection between the reader and the publisher, transforming passive consumption into an active relationship. The efficiency of this system is evident; instead of scouring multiple websites, the day's essential headlines and analyses arrive in a single, digestible format. As media outlets continue to prioritize direct audience relationships in a fragmented digital landscape, the humble email subscription, confirmed by that immediate note of gratitude, remains a surprisingly powerful and resilient tool for both informing the public and sustaining journalistic enterprises.

This victory marks a significant milestone, as Rumor becomes only the second German shepherd ever to claim Westminster's top honor, following the legendary Ch. Covy Tucker Hill's Manhattan in 1987. Her win is a testament to the breed's classic virtues of intelligence, structure, and athleticism, showcased perfectly in her confident and powerful gait around the famed green carpet. The decision by judge Dr. Thomas H. Bradley concluded a two-day marathon of competition that began with breed-specific judging in Piers 92/94 before moving to the Garden for the group finals. Rumor first secured the Herding Group title, a category historically dominated by German shepherds, before facing the winners from six other groups in the final ring. Her triumph was particularly poignant for the German shepherd community, which had waited three decades to see the breed ascend to the pinnacle of the dog show world once more. The victory also highlights the meticulous breeding and dedicated conditioning behind top show dogs; Rumor is the product of a successful breeding program and has been a standout on the circuit, consistently winning major shows leading up to Westminster. As the new champion, Rumor now retreats from the rigors of the show ring to enjoy a life of leisure, though her legacy will undoubtedly influence the breed for years to come. Her name will now be forever etched alongside the other greats in the Westminster Kennel Club's storied annals.
